sections.title: Temporal Projection, Precognition, and Causal-Calculus Canon
sections.explanation: This section establishes the cognitive/metacognitive measurement vocabulary used by the later causal-calculus material. It separates raw cognitive capacity from deployability, efficiency, proficiency, agility, power, and speed, then mirrors those distinctions at the metacognitive layer. The closing Arthitean rule couples corresponding cognitive and metacognitive capacities by Lydrextent, so the terms here are not interchangeable labels: they are distinct axes whose relationship is explicitly constrained.

paragraph_explanations.explanation: Defines capacity as a reserve rather than an observed performance; this distinction is needed because later metrics divide or compare capacities.
Fixes 'cognitive' to the act/domain of thinking, providing the base domain for the following measurements.
Defines metacognition as thinking about thinking, establishing a higher-order domain parallel to cognition.
Repeats the capacity definition; its recurrence reinforces that the same reserve-concept applies when cognitive and metacognitive quantities are compared.
Introduces cognitive efficiency as goal/task effectiveness relative to cognitive-capacity use; it is an economy-of-use measure, not total capacity.
Completes the preceding ratio by specifying the denominator: extent of cognitive-capacity usage.
Defines cognitive capacity as what the thinker is capable of doing cognitively; this is the resource ceiling against which deployment can be assessed.
Separates deployability from possession: Cognitive Deployability is how efficiently existing cognitive capacities can actually be brought to bear on tasks/goals.
Defines proficiency as deployability per cognitive capacity, explicitly warning that the denominator is capacity rather than a narrower notion of ability.
Defines agility as ease/speed of changing what or how one thinks; it concerns cognitive reconfiguration rather than throughput.
Defines cognitive power as the full extent of processing power available/exhibitable, distinct from efficiency or agility.
Defines cognitive speed as the full extent of processing speed, separating rate from power and deployability.

Introduces a two-source failure taxonomy: failure can arise from insufficient capacity or from deployment error. The parenthetical request for examples is preserved as an unresolved source note rather than silently completed here.
Starts the metacognitive mirror of cognitive efficiency: effectiveness in metathinking tasks/goals relative to metacognitive resource use.
Completes the metacognitive-efficiency ratio by specifying use of metacognitive capacities as the denominator.
Defines metacognitive capacity as what one is capable of doing in metathinking; it is the higher-order counterpart of cognitive capacity.
Defines metacognitive deployability as efficient use of metacognitive capacities, preserving the possession-versus-use distinction at the meta-level.
Defines metacognitive proficiency as deployability per metacognitive capacity, mirroring the cognitive proficiency construction.
Defines metacognitive power as total metathinking processing power, a magnitude axis separate from speed/agility/efficiency.
Defines metacognitive speed as total metathinking processing speed.
Defines metacognitive agility as the ease/speed of changing metathought, directly paralleling cognitive agility.

Adds the Arthitean coupling rule: where a cognitive capacity has a metacognitive counterpart, their extents are equated by Lydrextent. This is a cross-layer scaling constraint, not a claim that cognition and metacognition are identical.

evidence.basis: The closing Arthitean coupling rule explicitly uses Lydrextent.
